instruction: Build the sentence: a past habit that has stopped.
answer: I used to play football every weekend
explanation: 'Used to + verb' describes a habit that was true in the past but is not anymore.

instruction: Build the sentence: an action happening right now.
answer: She is writing a letter to her grandmother
explanation: The present continuous (is + -ing) describes an action in progress at this moment.

instruction: Build the sentence: comparing two things that are equal.
answer: This coffee is as strong as the one yesterday
explanation: 'As + adjective + as' makes an equal comparison: 'as strong as'.

instruction: Build the sentence: something that has never happened to you.
answer: I have never eaten durian ice cream
explanation: 'Have never + past participle' describes an experience that has not happened in your life so far.

instruction: Build the sentence: a polite request.
answer: Could you open the window please
explanation: 'Could you ...' is a polite request, softer than 'Can you ...'.

instruction: Build the sentence: a past action interrupted by another.
answer: I was cooking dinner when the phone rang
explanation: Past continuous (was cooking) for the longer background action, simple past (rang) for the interruption.

instruction: Build the sentence: an unreal wish about the present.
answer: I wish I had more free time
explanation: After 'I wish' about the present, use the past tense (had) to show the situation is unreal.

instruction: Build the sentence: something you regret about the past.
answer: I should have studied harder for the exam
explanation: 'Should have + past participle' expresses regret about something you did not do.

instruction: Build the sentence: a first conditional about tomorrow.
answer: If it rains tomorrow we will stay home
explanation: First conditional: present simple in the if-clause (rains), 'will' in the result clause.

instruction: Build the sentence: an imaginary situation about the future.
answer: If I won the lottery I would travel the world
explanation: Second conditional: past tense (won) for the unreal condition, 'would' for the imagined result.

instruction: Build the sentence: reported speech about a past promise.
answer: He said he would call me that evening
explanation: In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and 'this' often becomes 'that'.

instruction: Build the sentence: the passive voice about a famous building.
answer: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889
explanation: Passive voice: 'was + past participle' when the doer is unknown or unimportant.

instruction: Build the sentence: something that has been true since a starting point.
answer: We have lived in this house since 2018
explanation: Present perfect with 'since' + a starting point: the situation continues now.

instruction: Build the sentence: an action that will be finished before a future time.
answer: By next Friday I will have finished the project
explanation: Future perfect (will have + past participle): completed before a point in the future.

instruction: Build the sentence: advice with 'had better'.
answer: You had better leave now or you will miss the bus
explanation: 'Had better + base verb' gives strong advice about the near future. No 'to' after it.

instruction: Build the sentence: a cause-and-effect link with 'because'.
answer: She passed the test because she practised every day
explanation: 'Because' introduces the reason. Keep both verbs in the same past timeframe.

instruction: Build the sentence: a contrast between two ideas.
answer: He is very rich but he lives a simple life
explanation: 'But' joins two clauses that contrast with each other.

instruction: Build the sentence: something you are about to do.
answer: I am about to send the email
explanation: 'Be about to + verb' means the action will happen very soon.

instruction: Build the sentence: a past habit with 'would'.
answer: Every summer we would drive to the beach
explanation: 'Would + verb' can describe repeated past habits, just like 'used to', but never for states.

instruction: Build the sentence: an indirect question, polite form.
answer: Could you tell me where the station is
explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order (where the station IS), unlike direct questions (where IS the station).

instruction: Build the sentence: permission in the past.
answer: When I was young we were allowed to stay out late
explanation: 'Were allowed to' is the past of 'can' for permission.

instruction: Build the sentence: a superlative about a place.
answer: This is the most beautiful beach I have ever seen
explanation: Superlative (the most beautiful) plus 'I have ever seen' makes a strong personal claim.

instruction: Build the sentence: purpose with 'so that'.
answer: She spoke slowly so that everyone could understand
explanation: 'So that + could/would' explains the purpose of an action.

instruction: Build the sentence: a condition with 'unless'.
answer: We will lose the game unless we concentrate
explanation: 'Unless' means 'if ... not'. It takes the present tense, like any if-clause.

instruction: Build the sentence: something finished a short time ago.
answer: I have just finished my homework
explanation: 'Have just + past participle' means the action ended moments ago.

instruction: Build the sentence: emphasis with 'It was ... that'.
answer: It was my sister who broke the vase
explanation: The cleft sentence 'It was X who/that ...' highlights one part of the sentence.

instruction: Build the sentence: an obligation that is not being followed.
answer: You should be revising instead of playing games
explanation: 'Should be + -ing' criticises an action that should be happening right now but is not.

instruction: Build the sentence: no sooner ... than.
answer: No sooner had he arrived than the meeting started
explanation: 'No sooner had + subject + past participle + than' is a formal way to say one thing happened immediately after another.

instruction: Build the sentence: an unreal past with the third conditional.
answer: If we had left earlier we would have caught the train
explanation: Third conditional: 'if + past perfect' with 'would have + past participle' for an impossible past change.

instruction: Build the sentence: a tag question checking agreement.
answer: You have finished your assignment haven't you
explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag: 'you have ... haven't you'.

instruction: Build the sentence: a future arrangement already made.
answer: I am meeting the manager at three o'clock
explanation: Present continuous is used for fixed future appointments.

instruction: Build the sentence: a reason with 'because of' + noun.
answer: The flight was delayed because of the storm
explanation: 'Because of' takes a noun (the storm); 'because' takes a full clause (because there was a storm).

instruction: Build the sentence: something that is probably true now.
answer: She must be very tired after such a long flight
explanation: 'Must be' expresses a confident logical guess about the present.

instruction: Build the sentence: a polite offer.
answer: Would you like me to help with the dishes
explanation: 'Would you like me to ...' is a natural, polite way to offer help.

instruction: Build the sentence: past obligation with 'had to'.
answer: When I worked in Tokyo I had to wake up at five
explanation: 'Must' has no past form; use 'had to' for past obligation.

instruction: Build the sentence: something that needs doing.
answer: My hair needs cutting
explanation: After 'need', the -ing form has a passive meaning: 'needs cutting' = 'needs to be cut'.

instruction: Build the sentence: expressing preference.
answer: I would rather walk than take the bus
explanation: 'Would rather + verb + than + verb' compares two options you prefer between.

instruction: Build the sentence: a formal apology.
answer: I apologise for not replying sooner
explanation: After 'for' in apologies, use the -ing form: 'for not replying'.

instruction: Build the sentence: an action in progress in the past.
answer: While they were arguing the guests started leaving
explanation: 'While + past continuous' sets the background for a shorter past event.

instruction: Build the sentence: an invitation in the future.
answer: Would you like to join us for dinner tonight
explanation: 'Would you like to ...' is the standard polite invitation formula.

instruction: Build the sentence: a quantity expression with an uncountable noun.
answer: There is very little time left
explanation: 'Little' goes with uncountable nouns (time), 'few' with countable ones (minutes).

instruction: Build the sentence: someone said something surprising.
answer: Not only did she win but she also broke the record
explanation: When 'not only' starts the sentence, invert: 'Not only DID she win'.

instruction: Build the sentence: a deduction about the past.
answer: The roads are wet so it must have rained
explanation: 'Must have + past participle' is a confident guess about a past event.

instruction: Build the sentence: a complaint about an ongoing situation.
answer: This is the third time the train has been late this week
explanation: After 'this is the ... time', use the present perfect: 'has been late'.

instruction: Build the sentence: a general truth.
answer: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius
explanation: The present simple states facts that are always true.

instruction: Build the sentence: a formal request in writing.
answer: I would be grateful if you could send the report
explanation: 'I would be grateful if you could ...' is one of the politest request forms in written English.

instruction: Build the sentence: an action too difficult to do.
answer: The box was too heavy for me to lift
explanation: 'Too + adjective + for someone + to + verb' shows something exceeds ability.

instruction: Build the sentence: enough with an adjective.
answer: Is the room warm enough for you
explanation: 'Adjective + enough' (warm enough), never 'enough warm', comes after the adjective.

instruction: Build the sentence: what someone is said to be doing.
answer: He is said to be working on a new novel
explanation: 'Is said to be ...' is a formal reporting structure meaning 'people say he is ...'.

instruction: Build the sentence: a memory that keeps returning.
answer: I keep thinking about what she said
explanation: 'Keep + -ing' describes an action that repeats annoyingly or persistently.
